438:         <!-- WHAT IS CUSTOM LUXURY FURNITURE -->
439:         <div class="section-block">
440:             <h2 class="section-title">What Is Custom Luxury Furniture, and Why Does It Matter in Dubai?</h2>
441:             <p>Custom luxury furniture is furniture designed and built specifically for one space, rather than mass-produced and shipped in standard sizes. In Dubai, this distinction matters more than in most cities, because homes here vary enormously - a Palm Jumeirah villa, a Downtown Dubai apartment, and a Business Bay office suite each have completely different spatial and lifestyle demands.</p>
442:             <p><strong>Custom furniture solves three problems that ready-made pieces can't:</strong></p>
443:             <ul class="custom-list">
444:                 <li><strong>Fit</strong> — sectionals, wardrobes, and wall panels built to a room's exact measurements, including awkward corners and non-standard ceiling heights common in luxury developments.</li>
445:                 <li><strong>Material control</strong> — choosing solid hardwood, imported marble, or genuine leather instead of settling for whatever a catalog offers.</li>
446:                 <li><strong>Design cohesion</strong> — matching a home's architectural style (Italian-contemporary, modern minimalist, classic) across every room instead of mixing disconnected off-the-shelf pieces.</li>
447:             </ul>
448:         </div>
449: 
450:         <!-- POPULAR CATEGORIES WITH IMAGE 2 -->
451:         <div class="section-block">
452:             <h2 class="section-title">Popular Categories of Luxury Furniture in Dubai Homes</h2>
453:             <div class="content-grid reverse">
454:                 <div class="inline-img-box">
455:                     <img src="assets/images/home-page/bed-room.avif" alt="Custom Designer Living Room Furniture" loading="lazy">
456:                 </div>
457:                 <div>
458:                     <p>Most custom furniture requests in Dubai fall into a handful of categories:</p>
459:                     <p><strong>Designer Living Room Sets</strong><br>Italian-inspired modular sofas, custom L-shaped sectionals, recliners, marble coffee tables, and statement TV wall units.</p>
460:                     <p><strong>Luxury Bedroom Furniture</strong><br>King and queen designer beds, upholstered headboards, custom wardrobes, and full walk-in closet systems.</p>
461:                     <p><strong>Dining and Table Collections</strong><br>Marble-top and solid wood dining tables, extendable sets, and designer upholstered chairs.</p>
462:                 </div>
463:             </div>
464:             <p><strong>Wall Panels and Partitions</strong><br>Decorative and acoustic wall panels for villas, apartments, offices, and commercial interiors.</p>
465:             <p><strong>Bespoke and Made-to-Measure Pieces</strong><br>Built-in storage, space-saving solutions for compact apartments, and full villa furniture packages covering every room.</p>
466:         </div>
467: 
468:         <!-- MATERIALS THAT DEFINE LUXURY -->
469:         <div class="section-block">
470:             <h2 class="section-title">Which Materials Define True Luxury Furniture?</h2>
471:             <p>Not all "luxury" furniture is created equal. The material list is the clearest signal of quality — and it's worth asking any supplier exactly what they use. High-end Dubai furniture makers typically work with:</p>
472:             <ul class="custom-list">
473:                 <li>Solid hardwood for structural frames and longevity</li>
474:                 <li>Engineered wood for stability in humidity and temperature shifts</li>
475:                 <li>Imported marble for tabletops and statement surfaces</li>
476:                 <li>High-density foam for upholstery that holds its shape for years</li>
477:                 <li>Genuine leather for seating and headboards</li>
478:                 <li>High-grade metal fittings and hardware</li>
479:             </ul>
480:             <p>If a quote comes in significantly cheaper than competitors, it's usually because one of these materials has been substituted for a lower-grade alternative.</p>

589:                 <h1>Theyyampattil Furniture: The Story Behind the UAE's Bespoke Luxury Furniture Brand</h1>
590:                 <p class="excerpt">Theyyampattil Furniture has spent over four decades turning houses into bespoke homes — first in India, then across the UAE. This post breaks down the brand's history, its 100% in-house design-to-installation process, its showrooms in Dubai, Sharjah, and Abu Dhabi, and what makes it different from other luxury furniture brands in the region.</p>

600:                 <!-- Section 1: Who Is -->
601:                 <section class="section-block">
602:                     <h2>Who Is Theyyampattil Furniture?</h2>
603:                     <p>Walk into almost any conversation about custom furniture in Dubai, and the name Theyyampattil Furniture comes up fast. But most people who've seen the showrooms in Dubai, Sharjah, or Abu Dhabi don't actually know the story behind the brand where it started, how it grew, or what sets it apart from the dozens of other furniture retailers competing for the same customers. This post covers exactly that, so you know who you're dealing with before you set foot in a showroom.</p>
604:                     <p>Theyyampattil Furniture is a luxury home furniture brand offering custom-made pieces across the UAE, including <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">TV wall units</a>, <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">wardrobes</a>, <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">kitchens</a>, <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">bedroom sets</a>, and <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">wall panels</a>. What separates Theyyampattil Furniture from typical retailers is that design, manufacturing, and installation all happen in-house, giving every customer a fully bespoke result rather than a mass-produced item.</p>
605:                     <p>The brand currently operates three showrooms in the UAE - in <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">Dubai</a>, <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">Sharjah</a>, and <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/">Abu Dhabi</a> and is backed by more than 300 skilled designers and craftsmen.</p>
606:                 </section>

611:                     <div class="content-with-image">
612:                         <div>
613:                             <div class="sub-block">
614:                                 <h3>Founded in 1983</h3>
615:                                 <p>Theyyampattil Furniture traces its roots back to 1983 in India, where the founders set out to combine European design influences with traditional craftsmanship - treating each piece as part of a room's overall character rather than a standalone item. That approach earned the brand a strong reputation across the Indian subcontinent well before it ever touched Gulf shores.</p>
616:                             </div>
617:                             <div class="sub-block">
618:                                 <h3>Entering the UAE in 2000</h3>
619:                                 <p>In 2000, Theyyampattil Furniture crossed into the UAE market, recognizing the region's growing appetite for luxury, personalization, and contemporary living. Under Chairman Mr. Sharafudheen Theyyampattil and Managing Director Mr. Jahfar Sadiq, the brand has since grown into a genuine UAE furniture powerhouse.</p>
620:                             </div>
621:                         </div>

479: <!-- Hero Section -->
480: <section class="hero-section">
481:     <div class="hero-content">
482:         <h1 class="hero-title">Villa vs Apartment Furniture: Key Design Differences for UAE Homes</h1>
483:         <div class="hero-meta">
484:             Published on August 27, 2026 | By <a href="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Theyyampattil GCC</a>
485:         </div>
486:     </div>
487: </section>
488: 
489: <!-- Main Page Content Wrapper -->
490: <div class="page-container">
491:     <div class="content-wrapper">
492:         
493:         <!-- AEO / GEO Top Summary Box -->
494:         <div class="summary-box">
495:             <h3>Key Takeaway: Villa vs Apartment Furniture Strategy</h3>
496:             <p><strong>Quick Summary:</strong> Villa furniture in the UAE emphasizes grand scale, custom built-in joinery, and heavy natural materials for permanent multi-zone layouts. Apartment furniture prioritizes space-saving modular design, multi-functional utility, vertical storage, and lightweight silhouettes to navigate HOA building rules and compact footprints. Learn more about our custom furniture manufacturing services or explore our UAE interior portfolio.</p>
497:         </div>
498: 
499:         <!-- Intro Paragraphs -->
500:         <p>Villa furniture in the UAE is typically larger in scale, built-in, and designed around double-height ceilings and open-plan living, while apartment furniture favors modular, space-saving, and multi-functional pieces suited to compact layouts and building restrictions. Choosing the right approach depends on your property type, ceiling height, storage needs, and whether structural changes are allowed by your building or community.</p>
501:         
502:         <p>At Theyyampattil Furniture, we design and build for both villa owners across Dubai, Sharjah, and Abu Dhabi and apartment residents in high-rise communities and the two briefs are rarely the same. Here's exactly how they differ, and how to choose the right furniture strategy for your home.</p>
503: 
504:         <!-- Section 1 with Image Right -->
505:         <div class="flex-row">
506:             <div class="col-text">
507:                 <h2>Why Villas and Apartments Need Different Furniture Strategies</h2>
508:                 <p><strong>Direct Answer:</strong> A villa and an apartment require different furniture strategies because structural freedom, spatial volume, and ownership tenure dictate design. Furniture that looks stunning in a 5,000 sq ft villa can overwhelm a 1,200 sq ft apartment, and furniture that's efficient for apartment living can look sparse or under-scaled in a villa.</p>
509:                 <p>The three biggest factors that separate the two:</p>
510:                 <ul>
511:                     <li><strong>Space and ceiling height:</strong> villas often have double-height living rooms and larger footprints; apartments work within fixed, compact floor plans.</li>
512:                     <li><strong>Structural flexibility:</strong> villa owners can usually modify walls, built-ins, and layouts; apartment owners are often limited by building regulations set by municipal authorities like the <a href="https://www.dm.gov.ae/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="content-link">Dubai Municipality</a> and local HOA rules.</li>
513:                     <li><strong>Lifestyle and use:</strong> villas are designed for hosting, multi-generational living, and long-term permanence; apartments prioritize flexibility, storage efficiency, and easy resale or relocation.</li>
514:                 </ul>
515:             </div>
516:             <div class="col-image">
517:                 <img src="assets/images/home-page/tv-wall.avif" alt="Luxury Villa vs Apartment Interior Design Dubai" class="concise-img" width="800" height="280" loading="lazy" />
518:             </div>
519:         </div>
520: 
521:         <!-- Section 2: Villa Furniture with Image Left (Strict H2 -> H3 Hierarchy) -->
522:         <h2>Villa Furniture: Designing for Scale and Permanence</h2>
523:         
524:         <div class="flex-row reverse">
525:             <div class="col-text">
526:                 <h3>Furniture Scale Matches the Architecture</h3>
527:                 <p>Villas typically have higher ceilings and larger rooms, so furniture needs to be proportionally larger to avoid feeling lost in the space. Oversized sofas, statement dining tables, and taller wardrobe units are common in villa projects.</p>
528:                 <h3>Built-In and Custom Joinery Is the Default</h3>
529:                 <p>Because villa owners usually have full control over their interiors, built-in solutions walk-in closets, custom TV wall units, fitted kitchen cabinetry, and floor-to-ceiling wall panels are the standard rather than the exception. This allows every inch of a room to be tailored to the homeowner's exact measurements and lifestyle.</p>
530:             </div>
531:             <div class="col-image">
532:                 <img src="assets/images/home-page/kitchen.avif" alt="Custom Villa Built-in Joinery Dubai" class="concise-img" width="800" height="280" loading="lazy" />
533:             </div>
534:         </div>
535: 
536:         <h3>Multiple Living Zones Need Distinct Furniture Identities</h3>
537:         <p>A villa often includes a majlis, formal living room, family lounge, and outdoor terrace each with its own furniture language. A majlis calls for traditional, low-seating arrangements, while a family lounge favors comfort-first modern furniture.</p>
538: 
539:         <h3>Materials Can Be More Ambitious</h3>
540:         <p>With more space and typically higher budgets, villa furniture often uses premium natural materials - solid wood, natural stone finishes, and full-grain leathers - since there's room to let a single statement piece anchor a whole room.</p>
541: 
542:         <!-- GEO Original Experience / Case Study Proof -->
543:         <div class="proof-box">
544:             <h4>Real-World Case Benchmark: Palm Jumeirah Villa vs Business Bay Studio</h4>
545:             <p>In a recent 2026 project comparison executed by Theyyampattil design teams, our engineering measurements confirmed a 3.8-meter custom wall-paneling and solid marble dining unit installation in a 6,500 sq ft Palm Jumeirah villa required specialized load-bearing anchor testing. Conversely, in a 950 sq ft Business Bay apartment, we installed floor-to-ceiling modular joinery with integrated drop-down desks, yielding an audited 35% increase in usable floor area without triggering HOA structural penalties or altering core masonry.</p>
546:         </div>
547: 
548:         <!-- Section 3: Apartment Furniture (Strict H2 -> H3 Hierarchy) -->
549:         <h2>Apartment Furniture: Designing for Efficiency and Flexibility</h2>
550:         
551:         <div class="flex-row">
552:             <div class="col-text">
553:                 <h3>Every Piece Needs to Multi-Task</h3>
554:                 <p>In an apartment, a dining table might double as a workspace, and a storage ottoman might replace a coffee table entirely. Multi-functional furniture isn't a style choice it's a space necessity.</p>
555:                 <h3>Modular Beats Fixed</h3>
556:                 <p>Unlike villas, most apartments in Dubai and Abu Dhabi come with building restrictions on structural changes. Modular wardrobes, modular shelving, and freestanding TV units offer the custom look of built-ins without requiring permanent alterations and they move with you if you relocate.</p>
557:             </div>
558:             <div class="col-image">
559:                 <img src="https://theyyampattilgcc.com/assets/images/services/services-1-7.jpg" alt="Space Saving Apartment Modular Furniture" class="concise-img" width="800" height="280" loading="lazy" />
560:             </div>
561:         </div>
562: 
563:         <h3>Vertical Space Does the Heavy Lifting</h3>
564:         <p>With limited floor area, apartment furniture design leans on vertical storage tall, slim wardrobes, wall-mounted units, and ceiling-height shelving to maximize capacity without consuming floor space.</p>
565: 
566:         <h3>Light, Compact Silhouettes Keep Rooms Feeling Open</h3>
567:         <p>Bulky, deep furniture can make an apartment feel cramped. Slimmer profiles, lighter tones, and furniture raised slightly off the floor (visible legs rather than solid bases) help maintain an open, airy feel.</p>
568: 
569:         <!-- Section 4: Comparison Table -->
570:         <h2>Villa vs Apartment Furniture: Quick Comparison</h2>
571:         <div class="table-responsive">

649:             <div class="grid-2">
650:                 <div class="text-block">
651:                     <h2>What Is a Walk In Closet and Why <span>Dubai Homeowners Love Them</span></h2>
652:                     <p>Owning a premium home in Dubai, whether it is a villa on Palm Jumeirah, a high-rise penthouse in Downtown, or a residence in Jumeirah Golf Estates, comes with a certain standard. Every room reflects that standard. Your wardrobe space should be no different.</p>
653:                     <p>A walk in closet in Dubai is no longer just a storage room. It has become one of the most personal and high-value spaces in any premium residence, blending Italian craftsmanship, smart organization, and everyday luxury into a single room.</p>
654:                 </div>
655:                 <div class="text-block">
656:                     <p>Unlike a built-in wardrobe that you open and reach into, a walk in closet is a space you physically enter, move around in, and dress within. It is a dedicated room - separate from the bedroom - designed exclusively for storing, organizing, and displaying your clothing, shoes, bags, accessories, and jewelry.</p>
657:                     <p>At Theyyampattil Furniture, we have been designing and delivering custom luxury interiors across the UAE since 2000 - backed by a manufacturing legacy that began in 1983. With over 25 years of UAE experience, 1,000+ completed luxury projects, and showrooms in Dubai, Sharjah, and Abu Dhabi, we bring a level of craft and accountability that few providers in the region can match.</p>
658:                     <p>Our team of 300+ skilled designers, structural experts, and craftsmen handles everything in-house - from concept and manufacturing at our Sharjah and Abu Dhabi facilities to final installation at your property with no third-party subcontracting. This guide covers everything you need to know about walk in closets in Dubai, from layout planning and material selection to Dubai-specific design considerations and ideas suited to every type of luxury home.</p>
659:                 </div>
660:             </div>
661:         </div>
662:     </section>
663: 
664:     <section class="section-padding showcase-section">
665:         <div class="container">
666:             <div class="grid-2">
667:                 <div class="showcase-img">
668:                     <img src="assets/images/closets/closet-1.jpeg" alt="Modern Walk In Closet Boutique Design" width="544" height="680" loading="lazy">
669:                 </div>
670:                 <div class="text-block">
671:                     <h2>The Hallmark of <span>Luxury Living</span></h2>
672:                     <p>In Dubai, walk in closets have become a hallmark of luxury living for good reason. The city's residents are among the world's most fashion-forward, with extensive collections of designer clothing, high-end footwear, luxury handbags, and fine jewelry that deserve more than cramped shelving.</p>
673:                     <p>When designed properly, a walk in closet transforms your morning routine from a frustrating search into a calm, pleasurable experience - more like stepping into a high-end boutique than rummaging through a cupboard.</p>
674:                     <p>They also add measurable value to your property. In Dubai's competitive real estate market, a beautifully designed bespoke walk in closet is a genuine selling point, particularly in villas and penthouses where buyers expect a premium finish throughout.</p>
675:                     <p>Across more than a thousand luxury projects completed for local and expatriate families throughout the UAE, our teams at Theyyampattil have seen first-hand how a well-executed walk in closet elevates both daily life and long-term property value.</p>
676:                 </div>
677:             </div>
678:         </div>
679:     </section>
680: 
681:     <section class="section-padding">
682:         <div class="container">
683:             <h2>Key Design Elements of a <span>Luxury Walk In Closet</span> in Dubai</h2>
684:             <div class="elements-grid">
685:                 <div class="element-card">
686:                     <h3>Hanging Rails and Heights</h3>
687:                     <p>Not all hanging is equal. Dresses, coats, and full-length abayas require a single long rail with at least 170 cm of clearance. Shirts, folded trousers, and shorter jackets work well on double-hanging rails, which maximize vertical space by stacking two rows. In penthouses and villas with ceiling heights above 3.2 metres, pull-down mechanical rails allow you to use that extra height without stretching or climbing.</p>
688:                 </div>
689:                 <div class="element-card">
690:                     <h3>Drawer Configurations</h3>
691:                     <p>A great walk in closet has drawers in multiple depths - shallow ones for underwear and accessories, medium drawers for folded tops and trousers, and deep drawers for knitwear and heavier garments. Every drawer should have soft-close, full-extension runners. At least one drawer should be velvet-lined with built-in compartments for jewelry.</p>
692:                 </div>
693:                 <div class="element-card">
694:                     <h3>Shoe Storage</h3>
695:                     <p>Shoe storage is consistently under-planned. As a rule, always allow 20% more shelf space than you currently need, because collections grow. Women's heels and boxed shoes require more shelf height per row than men's shoes. For serious collectors, backlit glass-fronted shoe displays treated like a retail showcase are a popular luxury addition in Dubai walk in closets.</p>
696:                 </div>
697:                 <div class="element-card">
698:                     <h3>Bag and Accessory Storage</h3>
699:                     <p>Bags are the most neglected element in wardrobe design. Standard bags need open cubbies of varying sizes. Larger totes and travel bags need deeper compartments. Statement pieces - your most loved bags - deserve backlit display niches where they are showcased rather than hidden.</p>
700:                 </div>
701:                 <div class="element-card">
702:                     <h3>The Island Unit</h3>
703:                     <p>If there is one element worth investing in before everything else, it is the island. A properly sized island transforms the room from a wardrobe into a genuine dressing room. The top surface handles packing, folding, and outfit planning. The sides hold drawers for accessories, watches, and fragrances. A marble or leather-wrapped top adds a tactile luxury that you appreciate every single morning.</p>
704:                 </div>
705:                 <div class="element-card">
706:                     <h3>Lighting</h3>
707:                     <p>Lighting is where most walk in closets fail. The most common mistake is relying on a single overhead downlight, which creates harsh shadows and makes it nearly impossible to accurately judge fabric colour or outfit coordination. The right lighting specification for a Dubai walk in closet includes ambient dimmable downlights at 3000K colour temperature, LED strip lighting inside every cupboard, drawer, and shoe shelf that activates on opening, vertical illumination beside full-length mirrors - ideally wall sconces rather than overhead - and a high CRI (Colour Rendering Index) rating so that colours read accurately. This last point matters far more than most people realise. Poor lighting will make you look one way in your wardrobe and completely different in natural daylight.</p>
708:                 </div>
709:             </div>
710:         </div>
711:     </section>
712: 
713:     <section class="section-padding showcase-section">
714:         <div class="container">
715:             <div class="grid-2">
716:                 <div class="text-block">
717:                     <h2>Materials & Finishes: The <span>Theyyampattil Difference</span></h2>
718:                     <p>The quality gap between a standard fitted wardrobe and a genuine luxury walk in closet comes down primarily to materials, hardware, and finishing detail. At Theyyampattil Furniture, our walk in closets draw on Italian manufacturing traditions - the same heritage behind some of the world's most respected wardrobe and joinery brands. With in-house production facilities in Sharjah and Abu Dhabi and a team of over 300 skilled craftsmen, every component is manufactured, quality-checked, and installed entirely by our own people. There is no subcontracting, no quality compromise, and no accountability gap between what is designed and what is delivered. This end-to-end ownership is what our clients - rated us 4.7 to 4.9 stars across hundreds of verified Google reviews consistently highlight as the defining difference.</p>
719:                     <p>Carcass construction uses high-grade MDF and quality melamine interiors in light tones for maximum visibility, or warm oak-effect finishes for a richer aesthetic. Door finishes include real wood veneers in walnut, oak, and ash, high-gloss lacquer in any colour, and upholstered fabric panels for a softer, more residential feel. Glass-fronted doors are used in display zones where visibility is part of the design.</p>
720:                     <p>Hardware is where Italian craftsmanship truly shows. Brushed brass, antique bronze, matte black, and satin nickel handle options are available, along with push-to-open and finger-pull edge details for a fully handle-free aesthetic. Interior fittings include velvet-lined drawer dividers, pull-out tie and belt racks, valet rods, integrated laundry hampers, anti-tarnish jewellery tray liners, and cedar inserts in hanging zones for natural garment protection.</p>
721:                 </div>
722:                 <div class="showcase-img">
723:                     <img src="assets/images/closets/closet-2.jpeg" alt="Italian Craftsmanship Closet Materials Finishes" width="544" height="680" loading="lazy">
724:                 </div>
725:             </div>

729:     <section class="section-padding">
730:         <div class="container">
731:             <h2>Dubai-Specific Considerations <span>Every Walk In Closet Needs</span></h2>
732:             <div class="text-block">
733:                 <p>Designing a walk in closet in Dubai requires accounting for environmental factors that simply do not apply in most other parts of the world. This is knowledge that only comes from years of on-the-ground experience and with over 25 years of UAE project delivery behind us, it is something our design team at Theyyampattil builds into every brief from day one.</p>
734:             </div>
735:             <div class="elements-grid">
736:                 <div class="element-card">
737:                     <h3>Humidity and Climate Control</h3>
738:                     <p>Dubai's humidity levels, particularly during summer months, can damage natural fabrics, leather goods, and wooden hardware if the wardrobe is not properly climate controlled. The dressing room should sit within the air-conditioned zone of the master bedroom, maintaining a consistent temperature and stable humidity. Cedar inserts in drawers and hanging zones provide additional natural protection.</p>
739:                 </div>
740:                 <div class="element-card">
741:                     <h3>UV Protection</h3>
742:                     <p>South- and west-facing windows in a Dubai dressing room can expose clothing and bags to intense UV radiation during afternoon hours. If your layout includes such windows, motorised blackout drapes on a programmed scene are the practical solution. For display niches with LED lighting, UV-filtered museum-quality LEDs protect delicate textiles, leather, and fine materials.</p>
743:                 </div>
744:                 <div class="element-card">
745:                     <h3>Ventilation</h3>
746:                     <p>If your walk in closet does not have a window, a quiet exhaust fan on a humidistat prevents stagnant, moist air from building up a common cause of odour and fabric damage in windowless dressing rooms across Dubai apartments.</p>
747:                 </div>
748:                 <div class="element-card">
749:                     <h3>Scale of Dubai Luxury Properties</h3>
750:                     <p>Dubai's luxury villas and penthouses in areas such as Palm Jumeirah, Emirates Hills, Arabian Ranches, and Downtown Dubai often feature master suites large enough to accommodate generous, statement-level walk in closets. At Theyyampattil, we work regularly with these property types and understand how to design a closet that integrates with the scale and architecture of a high-end Dubai residence rather than feeling like an afterthought.</p>
751:                 </div>
752:             </div>
753:         </div>
754:     </section>
755: 
756:     <section class="section-padding showcase-section">
757:         <div class="container">
758:             <h2>Walk In Closet Ideas for <span>Different Dubai Homes</span></h2>
759:             <div class="location-grid">
760:                 <div class="location-card">
761:                     <h4>For Penthouse Apartments</h4>
762:                     <p>High ceilings are your greatest asset. Use them with pull-down rails, tall glass-fronted display units, and dramatic floor-to-ceiling joinery. A compact island and a well-specified dressing table make the space feel complete even in a moderately sized room.</p>
763:                 </div>
764:                 <div class="location-card">
765:                     <h4>For Palm Jumeirah and Emirates Hills Villas</h4>
766:                     <p>Space is rarely a constraint. Go for the full island layout with a his-and-hers dual zone. Invest in a marble island top, chandelier lighting, and a dedicated three-way full-length mirror. The dressing room should feel like a room in its own right - not a bonus storage space off the master.</p>
767:                 </div>
768:                 <div class="location-card">
769:                     <h4>For Downtown Dubai Apartments</h4>
770:                     <p>Space is more considered. A smart galley or U-shape layout maximises every square metre. Mirrored doors on one wall visually expand the room. Sliding wardrobe doors rather than hinged keep the floor space open and unobstructed.</p>
771:                 </div>
772:                 <div class="location-card">
773:                     <h4>For Arabian Ranches Family Villas</h4>
774:                     <p>Family walk in closets often need to work harder. Plan for two distinct zones, plenty of drawer depth, and robust hardware that handles daily heavy use across a busy household.</p>
775:                 </div>
776:             </div>
777:             <div class="center-showcase-img">
778:                 <img src="assets/images/closets/closet-3.jpeg" alt="Bespoke Walk In Closet Walkthrough View" width="1152" height="494" loading="lazy">
779:             </div>
780:         </div>
781:     </section>

783:     <section class="section-padding">
784:         <div class="container">
785:             <h2>Common Walk In Closet <span>Mistakes to Avoid</span> in Dubai</h2>
786:             <div class="text-block">
787:                 <p>Even well-intentioned designs can fall short. These are the most frequent mistakes we see in Dubai walk in closets - and that our team is regularly called in to correct and resolve on projects that were poorly planned or abandoned by other providers.</p>
788:             </div>
789:             <div class="mistakes-box">
790:                 <ul class="mistakes-list">
791:                     <li>Over-allocating long-hanging space when the wardrobe is mostly folded items this wastes more vertical space than any other planning error.</li>
792:                     <li>Under-providing for shoes - collections almost always grow, so build in more shelf space than you think you currently need.</li>
793:                     <li>Skipping the island in favour of more wall storage - you lose the functional heart of the room and the space never feels quite complete.</li>
794:                     <li>Defaulting to warm 2700K lighting - flattering in a living room, but it distorts colour and makes outfit selection genuinely difficult.</li>
795:                     <li>No power outlets near the dressing table for hair tools, makeup mirrors, and phone charging, this is a daily frustration that is trivially easy to solve at design stage and nearly impossible to fix after installation.</li>
796:                     <li>Fixed, non-adjustable shelving - your wardrobe will change over time, and your storage system should be able to change with it.</li>
797:                 </ul>
798:             </div>
799:         </div>
800:     </section>

312: <script>
313:   (function() {
314:     'use strict';
315:     
316:     let lastScrollY = window.scrollY;
317:     let ticking = false;
318:     let scrollTimer = null;
319:     let fabIcons = null;
320: 
321:     function init() {
322:       fabIcons = document.querySelectorAll('.fab-icon-wrapper');
323:       window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, { passive: true });
324:     }
325: 
326:     function onScroll() {
327:       if (!ticking) {
328:         requestAnimationFrame(updateIcons);
329:         ticking = true;
330:       }
331:       
332:       clearTimeout(scrollTimer);
333:       scrollTimer = setTimeout(resetIcons, 120);
334:     }
335: 
336:     function updateIcons() {
337:       const currentScroll = window.scrollY;
338:       const travel = currentScroll - lastScrollY;
339:       
340:       // Calculate dynamic rotation angle (-18deg to +18deg)
341:       const rotation = Math.min(Math.max(travel * 0.22, -18), 18); 
342:       const scale = 1 + Math.abs(rotation / 140);
343:       
344:       if (fabIcons) {
345:         for (let i = 0; i < fabIcons.length; i++) {
346:           fabIcons[i].style.transform = `translate3d(0,0,0) rotate(${rotation}deg) scale(${scale})`;
347:         }
348:       }
349:       
350:       lastScrollY = currentScroll;
351:       ticking = false;
352:     }
353: 
354:     function resetIcons() {
355:       if (fabIcons) {
356:         for (let i = 0; i < fabIcons.length; i++) {
357:           fabIcons[i].style.transform = 'translate3d(0,0,0) rotate(0deg) scale(1)';
358:         }
359:       }
360:     }
361: 
362:     if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
363:       document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', init);
364:     } else {
365:       init();
366:     }
367:   })();
368: </script>

  1: <?php
  2: // send-mail.php
  3: ini_set('display_errors', 1);
  4: ini_set('display_startup_errors', 1);
  5: error_reporting(E_ALL);
  6: 
  7: date_default_timezone_set('UTC');
  8: 
  9: // Load sensitive configuration settings from parent /includes directory
 10: $config = require dirname(__DIR__) . '/includes/config.php';
 11: 
 12: require_once __DIR__ . '/phpmailer/Exception.php';
 13: require_once __DIR__ . '/phpmailer/PHPMailer.php';
 14: require_once __DIR__ . '/phpmailer/SMTP.php';
 15: 
 16: use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\PHPMailer;
 17: use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception;
 18: 
 19: if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] !== 'POST') {
 20:     http_response_code(405);
 21:     echo "Method not allowed";
 22:     exit;
 23: }
 24: 
 25: if (!empty($_POST['hp'])) {
 26:     http_response_code(400);
 27:     echo "Spam detected";
 28:     exit;
 29: }
 30: 
 31: $name    = trim($_POST['name'] ?? '');
 32: $email   = trim($_POST['email'] ?? '');
 33: $phone   = trim($_POST['phone'] ?? '');
 34: $message = trim($_POST['message'] ?? '');
 35: 
 36: // -----------------------------
 37: // Server-side phone normalization (IMMEDIATE AGGRESSIVE FIX)
 38: // -----------------------------
 39: function normalize_phone($raw) {
 40:     $s = trim((string)$raw);
 41:     if ($s === '') return '';
 42: 
 43:     // Extract all numbers out of the string entirely
 44:     $digits = preg_replace('/\D+/', '', $s);
 45: 
 46:     // If it starts with 91 or +91 or is a 10-digit number that likely comes from India
 47:     if (strpos($s, '+91') === 0) {
 48:         return '+' . $digits;
 49:     }
 50:     if (strpos($digits, '91') === 0 && strlen($digits) >= 11) {
 51:         return '+' . $digits;
 52:     }
 53:     
 54:     // Strip leading zeros
 55:     $cleanDigits = preg_replace('/^0/', '', $digits);
 56:     if (strlen($cleanDigits) === 10) {
 57:         // If it's a raw 10 digit local number, assign it to India directly
 58:         return '+91' . $cleanDigits;
 59:     }
 60: 
 61:     // Handle other explicitly declared country prefixes 
 62:     if (strpos($digits, '971') === 0 && strlen($digits) >= 11) {

  1: # ======================================================================
  2: # APACHE CONFIGURATION FOR THEMAMPATTILGCC.COM
  3: # Optimizations: SEO, AI Engine Discovery, GTmetrix A Grade, Security & CLS Fixes
  4: # ======================================================================
  5: 
  6: RewriteEngine On
  7: 
  8: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  9: # 1. DEFAULT SERVER SETTINGS & ENCODING
 10: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 11: # Force UTF-8 to prevent character rendering delays & layout jumping
 12: AddDefaultCharset UTF-8
 13: ServerSignature Off
 14: 
 15: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 16: # 2. SSL & WWW CANONICALIZATION (PRODUCTION ONLY)
 17: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 18: # Force HTTPS and non-WWW domain canonicalization
 19: RewriteCond %{HTTP_HOST} ^(www\.)?theyyampattilgcc\.com$ [NC]
 20: RewriteCond %{HTTPS} off [OR]
 21: RewriteCond %{HTTP_HOST} ^www\.theyyampattilgcc\.com$ [NC]
 22: RewriteRule ^(.*)$ https://theyyampattilgcc.com/$1 [L,R=301]
 23: 
 24: # Redirect direct index.php requests to root domain
 25: RewriteCond %{HTTP_HOST} ^(www\.)?theyyampattilgcc\.com$ [NC]
 26: RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} ^/index\.php$
 27: RewriteRule ^(.*)$ https://theyyampattilgcc.com/ [L,R=301]
 28: 
 29: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 30: # 3. URL STRUCTURE & TRAILING SLASH LOGIC
 31: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 32: # Exclude send-mail.php from all rewrite processing to preserve POST payloads
 33: RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} ^/send-mail\.php$ [NC]
 34: RewriteRule ^ - [L]
 35: 
 36: # A. Redirect direct /example.php requests to /example/
 37: RewriteCond %{THE_REQUEST} ^[A-Z]{3,}\s/+(.+)\.php[\s?] [NC]
 38: RewriteRule ^ /%1/ [R=301,L]
 39: 
 40: # B. Enforce Trailing Slash: Redirect /example to /example/
 41: # Excludes real files and real directories
 42: RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-f
 43: RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-d
 44: RewriteCond %{REQUEST_URI} !(.*)/$
 45: RewriteRule ^(.*)$ %{REQUEST_URI}/ [L,R=301]
 46: 
 47: # C. Internal Rewrite: Map /example/ internally to /example.php
 48: # Works seamlessly in subdirectories (localhost) and root domain (production)
 49: RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-d
 50: RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-f
 51: RewriteRule ^(.*)/$ $1.php [L]
 52: 
 53: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 54: # 4. GZIP / DEFLATE COMPRESSION (GTmetrix Performance)
 55: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 56: <IfModule mod_deflate.c>
 57:   # Compress HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Text, XML and Fonts
 58:   AddOutputFilterByType DEFLATE text/html text/plain text/xml text/css text/javascript
 59:   AddOutputFilterByType DEFLATE application/javascript application/x-javascript application/json
 60:   AddOutputFilterByType DEFLATE application/xml application/xhtml+xml application/rss+xml
 61:   AddOutputFilterByType DEFLATE application/vnd.ms-fontobject font/ttf font/otf font/opentype font/woff font/woff2
 62:   AddOutputFilterByType DEFLATE image/svg+xml image/x-icon
 63: </IfModule>
 64: 
 65: # Ensure CDNs and browsers serve correct compressed versions
 66: <IfModule mod_headers.c>
 67:   Header append Vary User-Agent env=!dont-vary
 68:   Header append Vary Accept-Encoding
 69: </IfModule>
 70: 
 71: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 72: # 5. BROWSER CACHING & CLS PREVENTATIVE EXPIRES HEADERS
 73: # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
 74: <IfModule mod_expires.c>
 75:   ExpiresActive On

 780:       (function(){
 781:         var counters = document.querySelectorAll('#stats-grid [data-target]');
 782:         var started = false;
 783:         function animateCounters(){
 784:           counters.forEach(function(el){
 785:             var target = parseInt(el.getAttribute('data-target'));
 786:             var suffix = el.getAttribute('data-suffix') || '';
 787:             var duration = 1800;
 788:             var start = performance.now();
 789:             function update(now){
 790:               var elapsed = now - start;
 791:               var progress = Math.min(elapsed / duration, 1);
 792:               var ease = 1 - Math.pow(1 - progress, 3);
 793:               el.textContent = Math.floor(ease * target) + suffix;
 794:               if(progress < 1) requestAnimationFrame(update);
 795:             }
 796:             requestAnimationFrame(update);
 797:           });
 798:         }
 799:         var observer = new IntersectionObserver(function(entries){
 800:           if(entries[0].isIntersecting && !started){
 801:             started = true;
 802:             animateCounters();
 803:           }
 804:         }, {threshold: 0.4});
 805:         observer.observe(document.getElementById('stats-grid'));
 806:       })();

================
File: send-mail.php
================
  1: <?php 
  2: session_start();
  3: 
  4: use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\PHPMailer;
  5: use PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Exception;
  6: 
  7: // Load sensitive configuration settings
  8: $config = require __DIR__ . '/includes/config.php';
  9: 
 10: // 1. Path Management: Ensure these files exist in your /PHPMailer/src/ directory
 11: require __DIR__ . '/PHPMailer/src/Exception.php';
 12: require __DIR__ . '/PHPMailer/src/PHPMailer.php';
 13: require __DIR__ . '/PHPMailer/src/SMTP.php';
 14: 
 15: // --- Server-Side Captcha Validation ---
 16: if ($_SERVER["REQUEST_METHOD"] == "POST") {
 17:     $user_captcha = isset($_POST['captcha_input']) ? trim($_POST['captcha_input']) : '';
 18:     $correct_captcha = isset($_SESSION['captcha_answer']) ? $_SESSION['captcha_answer'] : null;
 19: 
 20:     if ($correct_captcha === null || $user_captcha === '' || (int)$user_captcha !== (int)$correct_captcha) {
 21:         echo "invalid_captcha";
 22:         exit;
 23:     }
 24: }
 25: 
 26: $mail = new PHPMailer(true);
 27: 
 28: try {
 29:     // --- Server Settings ---
 30:     $mail->isSMTP();
 31:     $mail->Host       = $config['smtp']['host'];
 32:     $mail->SMTPAuth   = $config['smtp']['auth'];
 33:     
 34:     // SECURITY NOTE: Credentials loaded from includes/config.php
 35:     $mail->Username   = $config['smtp']['username'];
 36:     $mail->Password   = $config['smtp']['password']; 
 37:     
 38:     $mail->SMTPSecure = PHPMailer::ENCRYPTION_SMTPS; 
 39:     $mail->Port       = $config['smtp']['port'];
 40: 
 41:     // --- SSL Configuration ---
 42:     // Keep this only for local testing (XAMPP). 
 43:     // Remove the 'SMTPOptions' block entirely when moving to a live Linux server.
 44:     $mail->SMTPOptions = array(
 45:         'ssl' => array(
 46:             'verify_peer' => false,
 47:             'verify_peer_name' => false,
 48:             'allow_self_signed' => true
 49:         )
 50:     );
 51: 
 52:     // --- Recipients ---
 53:     $mail->setFrom($config['mail']['from_email'], $config['mail']['from_name']);
 54:     $mail->addAddress($config['mail']['to_email']); 
 55:     // $mail->addCC($config['mail']['from_email']);
 56:     
 57:     // --- Data Sanitization (Fixing XSS & Injection) ---
 58:     // Mandatory Fields (Name, Email, Phone, Subject)
 59:     $name    = isset($_POST['name']) ? htmlspecialchars(strip_tags(trim($_POST['name']))) : 'No Name';
 60:     $email   = filter_var($_POST['email'] ?? '', FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL) ? $_POST['email'] : 'Invalid Email';
 61:     $phone   = isset($_POST['phone']) ? htmlspecialchars(strip_tags(trim($_POST['phone']))) : 'No Phone';
 62:     
 63:     // Fallback support for subject (Case insensitive check)
 64:     $subject_input = $_POST['Subject'] ?? $_POST['subject'] ?? '';
 65:     $subject = !empty($subject_input) ? htmlspecialchars(strip_tags(trim($subject_input))) : 'New Website Inquiry';
 66:     
 67:     // Optional Field: Message (No error thrown if empty)
 68:     $raw_message = isset($_POST['message']) ? trim($_POST['message']) : '';
 69:     $message = !empty($raw_message) ? htmlspecialchars(strip_tags($raw_message)) : 'N/A';
 70:     
 71:     // Extra tracking parameters captured by intl-tel-input
 72:     $country_code = isset($_POST['country_code']) ? htmlspecialchars(strip_tags(trim($_POST['country_code']))) : '';
 73: 
 74:     // Mandatory Validation: Don't send if email, name, or phone is invalid/empty
 75:     if ($email === 'Invalid Email') {
 76:         throw new Exception("Please provide a valid email address.");
 77:     }
 78: 
 79:     if (empty($name) || $name === 'No Name') {
 80:         throw new Exception("Please provide your name.");
 81:     }
 82: 
 83:     if (empty($phone) || $phone === 'No Phone') {
 84:         throw new Exception("Please provide your phone number.");
 85:     }
 86: 
 87:     // Set reply-to header so clicking "Reply" responds directly to the user
 88:     $mail->addReplyTo($email, $name);
 89: 
 90:     // --- Email Content ---
 91:     $mail->isHTML(true);
 92:     $mail->Subject = "New Contact form Inquiry from website theyyampattilgcc.com: " . $subject;
 93:     
 94:     // HTML Email Body
 95:     $mail->Body = "
 96:         <h3>New contact form enquiry from website theyyampattilgcc.com</h3>
 97:         <p><strong>Name:</strong> {$name}</p>
 98:         <p><strong>Email:</strong> {$email}</p>
 99:         <p><strong>Phone:</strong> {$phone} " . (!empty($country_code) ? "({$country_code})" : "") . "</p>
100:         <p><strong>Subject:</strong> {$subject}</p>
101:         <p><strong>Message:</strong><br>" . nl2br($message) . "</p>
102:     ";
103:     
104:     // Plain text version for non-HTML mail clients
105:     $mail->AltBody = "Name: $name\nEmail: $email\nPhone: $phone " . (!empty($country_code) ? "($country_code)" : "") . "\nSubject: $subject\nMessage: $message";
106: 
107:     $mail->send();
108:     
109:     // Clear the evaluated captcha answer out of session memory upon a clean send
110:     unset($_SESSION['captcha_answer']);
111:     unset($_SESSION['captcha_num1']);
112:     unset($_SESSION['captcha_num2']);
113:     unset($_SESSION['captcha_operator']);
114:     
115:     echo "success";
116: 
117: } catch (Exception $e) {
118:     // Return error response for AJAX handler
119:     echo "Message could not be sent. Mailer Error: {$mail->ErrorInfo}";
120: }
121: ?>

617:         // Smooth Responsive Accordion Logic
618:         document.querySelectorAll('.accrodion-title').forEach(title => {
619:             title.addEventListener('click', () => {
620:                 const parent = title.parentElement;
621:                 const wasActive = parent.classList.contains('active');
622:                 
623:                 document.querySelectorAll('.accrodion').forEach(acc => {
624:                     acc.classList.remove('active');
625:                     const btn = acc.querySelector('.accrodion-title');
626:                     if (btn) btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
627:                 });
628:                 
629:                 if (!wasActive) {
630:                     parent.classList.add('active');
631:                     title.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
632:                 }
633:             });
634:         });

744:             <div class="guide-box">
745:                 <h2 class="section-title" style="font-size: 1.8rem; margin-bottom: 20px;">How to Choose the Right TV Wall Unit for Your Living Room</h2>
746:                 <p style="color: var(--text-gray); margin-bottom: 24px;">Picking a TV wall unit isn't just about matching your sofa—it's about the room's layout, your storage needs, and how the space is used day to day. A few things worth thinking through before you order a custom TV unit in UAE:</p>
747:                 
748:                 <div class="guide-item">
749:                     <h3>Measure your wall and viewing distance first</h3>
750:                     <p>The width of your TV wall unit should generally be close to the width of your TV console area, and the screen's center should sit at eye level when seated. For most Dubai living rooms, this means a floating or low-profile unit works better than a tall cabinet, which can crowd the sightline.</p>
751:                 </div>
752:                 
753:                 <div class="guide-item">
754:                     <h3>Decide how much storage you actually need</h3>
755:                     <p>If you store gaming consoles, routers, décor, or books in the living room, a storage-rich TV cabinet with concealed compartments keeps cables and clutter out of sight. If the room is minimal by design, a slim floating TV mount with little to no cabinetry often looks cleaner.</p>
756:                 </div>
757:                 
758:                 <div class="guide-item">
759:                     <h3>Match the finish to the rest of the room</h3>
760:                     <p>A wooden TV unit warms up a room with cooler tones (marble floors, grey walls), while a marble-finish TV unit pairs well with warmer wood flooring or a more traditional interior. Mixing one accent material (like a marble strip or wood-slat panel) is usually enough - using both throughout tends to compete rather than complement.</p>
761:                 </div>
762:                 
763:                 <div class="guide-item">
764:                     <h3>Think about lighting early, not as an afterthought</h3>
765:                     <p>Integrated LED lighting is far easier and neater to plan into a custom TV unit at the design stage than to retrofit later. If you want a warm, ambient look in the evening, mention it when you're discussing the design—it changes where cables and drivers need to be routed inside the unit.</p>
766:                 </div>
767:                 
768:                 <div class="guide-item">
769:                     <h3>Don't skip cable and ventilation planning</h3>
770:                     <p>Behind almost every TV wall unit issue we get called out to fix later is poor cable routing or a lack of ventilation behind enclosed electronics. A well-designed custom TV unit builds in cable channels and vents from the start, so your setup stays tidy and your equipment doesn't overheat.</p>
771:                 </div>
772:             </div>

644:     <script>
645:         function openFullView(pdfUrl, title) {
646:             const modal = new bootstrap.Modal(document.getElementById('pdfModal'));
647:             
648:             let finalUrl = pdfUrl + '#view=FitH';
649:             if (window.innerWidth < 992) {
650:                 finalUrl = 'https://docs.google.com/viewer?url=https://theyyampattilgcc.com/' + pdfUrl + '&embedded=true';
651:             }
652: 
653:             document.getElementById('modalIframe').src = finalUrl;
654:             document.getElementById('modalTitle').innerText = title;
655:             document.getElementById('modalDownloadBtn').href = pdfUrl;
656:             modal.show();
657:         }
658:         
659:         document.getElementById('pdfModal').addEventListener('hidden.bs.modal', function () {
660:             document.getElementById('modalIframe').src = '';
661:         });
662:     </script>

654:             zoomable: true,

658:         // Clickable FAQ Accordion Interactivity
659:         document.querySelectorAll('.faq-question').forEach(button => {
660:             button.addEventListener('click', () => {
661:                 const faqItem = button.parentElement;
662:                 const isOpen = faqItem.classList.contains('active');
663: 
664:                 // Close all FAQ items
665:                 document.querySelectorAll('.faq-item').forEach(item => {
666:                     item.classList.remove('active');
667:                     item.querySelector('.faq-question').setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
668:                 });
669: 
670:                 // Open clicked item if it was closed
671:                 if (!isOpen) {
672:                     faqItem.classList.add('active');
673:                     button.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
674:                 }
675:             });
676:         });

571:     document.querySelectorAll('.faq-question').forEach(button => {
572:         button.addEventListener('click', () => {
573:             const faqItem = button.parentElement;
574:             const isOpen = faqItem.classList.contains('active');
575:             
576:             // Close all items
577:             document.querySelectorAll('.faq-item').forEach(item => {
578:                 item.classList.remove('active');
579:                 item.querySelector('.faq-question').setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
580:             });
581: 
582:             // Open clicked item if it was not open
583:             if (!isOpen) {
584:                 faqItem.classList.add('active');
585:                 button.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
586:             }
587:         });
588:     });

358:     (function(){
359:       var h=document.getElementById('site-header'),
360:           t=document.getElementById('navToggle'),
361:           m=document.getElementById('mobileNav'),
362:           ticking=false;
363: 
364:       /* Scroll: throttled via rAF */
365:       function onScroll(){
366:         if(!ticking){
367:           requestAnimationFrame(function(){
368:             h.classList.toggle('scrolled',window.scrollY>60);
369:             ticking=false;
370:           });
371:           ticking=true;
372:         }
373:       }
374:       window.addEventListener('scroll',onScroll,{passive:true});
375: 
376:       /* Hamburger toggle */
377:       t.addEventListener('click',function(){
378:         var open=m.classList.toggle('open');
379:         t.classList.toggle('active',open);
380:         t.setAttribute('aria-expanded',open);
381:         document.body.style.overflow=open?'hidden':'';
382:       });
383: 
384:       /* Close mobile nav on link click */
385:       m.querySelectorAll('a').forEach(function(a){
386:         a.addEventListener('click',function(){
387:           m.classList.remove('open');
388:           t.classList.remove('active');
389:           t.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');
390:           document.body.style.overflow='';
391:         });
392:       });
393: 
394:       /* Close on resize to desktop */
395:       window.addEventListener('resize',function(){
396:         if(window.innerWidth>1024&&m.classList.contains('open')){
397:           m.classList.remove('open');
398:           t.classList.remove('active');
399:           t.setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');
400:           document.body.style.overflow='';
401:         }
402:       },{passive:true});
403:     })();
404:   </script>

372:         let globalSlideIndex = 0;
373: 
374:         function startMasterSyncSlide() {
375:             setInterval(() => {
376:                 globalSlideIndex++;
377:                 const wrappers = document.querySelectorAll('.sync-wrapper');
378:                 
379:                 wrappers.forEach((wrapper, i) => {
380:                     const p = products[i];
381:                     if (!p || p.imgs.length <= 1) return;
382: 
383:                     const totalImgs = p.imgs.length;
384:                     const localIndex = globalSlideIndex % totalImgs;
385:                     
386:                     const movePercentage = localIndex * (100 / totalImgs);
387:                     wrapper.style.transform = `translateX(-${movePercentage}%)`;
388:                     
389:                     const container = wrapper.closest('.img-container');
390:                     const dots = container.querySelectorAll('.dot');
391:                     dots.forEach((d, idx) => {
392:                         if(idx === localIndex) {
393:                             d.classList.add('bg-[#c5a367]', 'scale-125');
394:                             d.classList.remove('bg-white/30');
395:                         } else {
396:                             d.classList.remove('bg-[#c5a367]', 'scale-125');
397:                             d.classList.add('bg-white/30');
398:                         }
399:                     });
400:                 });
401:             }, 3500);
402:         }
403:

411:                     <div class="w-full flex justify-between items-center py-4 border-b border-white/10 mb-6">
412:                         <div>
413:                             <h4 class="text-white font-bold text-lg">${product.name}</h4>
414:                             <p class="text-[#c5a367] text-xs">${product.tag}</p>
415:                         </div>
416:                         <button onclick="closeLightbox()" class="bg-white text-black px-6 py-2 rounded-xl font-bold uppercase text-xs shadow-2xl hover:bg-[#c5a367] transition-all">
417:                             ✕ Close Inventory
418:                         </button>
419:                     </div>

514:     <script>
515:     window.addEventListener('load', () => {
516:         const phoneInput = document.querySelector("#phone");
517:         const countryHidden = document.querySelector("#country_code");
518:         const form = document.querySelector("#furniture-form");
519:         const submitBtn = document.querySelector("#submit-btn");
520:         const responseMsg = document.querySelector("#form-response-msg");
521:         
522:         let iti = null;
523:         if (window.intlTelInput && phoneInput) {
524:             iti = window.intlTelInput(phoneInput, {
525:                 initialCountry: "auto",
526:                 geoIpLookup: function(success, failure) {
527:                     fetch('https://ipinfo.io/json').then(res => res.json()).then(data => {
528:                         success(data.country);
529:                         if (countryHidden) countryHidden.value = data.country.toUpperCase();
530:                     }).catch(() => {
531:                         success("ae");
532:                         if (countryHidden) countryHidden.value = "AE";
533:                     });
534:                 },
535:                 utilsScript: "https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/intl-tel-input/17.0.8/js/utils.js",
536:             });
537:         }
538: 
539:         if(form) {
540:             form.addEventListener('submit', function(e) {
541:                 e.preventDefault();
542:                 
543:                 if (iti && phoneInput) {
544:                     phoneInput.value = iti.getNumber(); 
545:                 }
546: 
547:                 if (submitBtn) {
548:                     submitBtn.disabled = true;
549:                     submitBtn.innerHTML = 'Sending...';
550:                 }
551: 
552:                 if (responseMsg) {
553:                     responseMsg.classList.add('hidden');
554:                     responseMsg.innerText = '';
555:                 }
556: 
557:                 const formData = new FormData(form);
558: 
559:                 fetch(form.getAttribute('action'), {
560:                     method: 'POST',
561:                     body: formData
562:                 })
563:                 .then(res => {
564:                     if (res.redirected) {
565:                         window.location.href = res.url;
566:                         return null; // FIXED: Kill the promise chain if we are redirecting
567:                     }
568:                     return res.text();
569:                 })
570:                 .then(data => {
571:                     if (data === null) return; // FIXED: Prevent `undefined` error if redirected
572: 
573:                     if (submitBtn) {
574:                         submitBtn.disabled = false;
575:                         submitBtn.innerHTML = 'Submit Request';
576:                     }
577:                     if (responseMsg) {
578:                         responseMsg.classList.remove('hidden');
579:                         if (data && data.toLowerCase().includes('success')) {
580:                             responseMsg.className = 'text-xs text-center font-bold mt-2 text-emerald-400';
581:                             responseMsg.innerText = 'Thank you! Your request has been sent successfully.';
582:                             form.reset();
583:                         } else {
584:                             // FIXED: Added absolute path to prevent recursive folder stacking
585:                             window.location.href = '/store/thank-you.php';
586:                         }
587:                     }
588:                 })
589:                 .catch(err => {
590:                     if (submitBtn) {
591:                         submitBtn.disabled = false;
592:                         submitBtn.innerHTML = 'Submit Request';
593:                     }
594:                     if (responseMsg) {
595:                         responseMsg.classList.remove('hidden');
596:                         responseMsg.className = 'text-xs text-center font-bold mt-2 text-rose-400';
597:                         responseMsg.innerText = 'Network error. Please try again.';
598:                     }
599:                 });
600:             });
601:         }
602: 
603:         if (window.gsap && window.ScrollTrigger) {
604:             gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger);
605:             gsap.from(".bg-[#1e1e1e]", {
606:                 scrollTrigger: { trigger: "#products", start: "top 85%" },
607:                 y: 30,
608:                 opacity: 0,
609:                 duration: 0.8,
610:                 stagger: 0.08,
611:                 ease: "power2.out"
612:             });
613:         }
614:     });
615:     </script>
616: </body>
617: </html>

 625:   <script>
 626:     document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
 627:       const slides = document.querySelectorAll('.hero-slide');
 628:       const dots = document.querySelectorAll('.hero-dot');
 629:       let current = 0;
 630:       let timer;
 631: 
 632:       function goToSlide(n){
 633:         slides[current].classList.remove('active');
 634:         dots[current].classList.remove('active');
 635:         current = (n + slides.length) % slides.length;
 636:         slides[current].classList.add('active');
 637:         dots[current].classList.add('active');
 638:         resetTimer();
 639:       }
 640: 
 641:       function resetTimer() {
 642:         clearInterval(timer);
 643:         timer = setInterval(() => {
 644:           requestAnimationFrame(() => goToSlide(current + 1));
 645:         }, 6000);
 646:       }
 647: 
 648:       window.addEventListener('load', () => {
 649:         const otherImages = [
 650:           'assets/images/home-page/hero-banner/hero-slider-2.avif'
 651:         ];
 652:         otherImages.forEach(src => {
 653:           const img = new Image();
 654:           img.src = src;
 655:         });
 656:       }, {passive: true});
 657: 
 658:       window.goToSlide = goToSlide;
 659:       resetTimer();
 660:     });
 661:   </script>

2649:   <script>
2650:     function toggleFaq(btn) {
2651:       const isExpanded = btn.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true';
2652:       const allBtns = document.querySelectorAll('.faq-q');
2653:       
2654:       allBtns.forEach(otherBtn => {
2655:         if (otherBtn !== btn && otherBtn.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true') {
2656:           otherBtn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
2657:           otherBtn.nextElementSibling.style.maxHeight = '0';
2658:         }
2659:       });
2660: 
2661:       const content = btn.nextElementSibling;
2662:       if (!isExpanded) {
2663:         btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
2664:         content.style.maxHeight = content.scrollHeight + "px";
2665:       } else {
2666:         btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
2667:         content.style.maxHeight = '0';
2668:       }
2669:     }
2670:   </script>

2917:   <script>
2918:     function initTestimonialSlider() {
2919:       const track = document.getElementById('testimonialsTrack');
2920:       const prevBtn = document.getElementById('tstPrev');
2921:       const nextBtn = document.getElementById('tstNext');
2922:       const dotsContainer = document.getElementById('tstDots');
2923:       const cards = document.querySelectorAll('.testimonial-card');
2924:       let currentIndex = 0;
2925: 
2926:       function getVisibleCards() {
2927:         if (window.innerWidth <= 600) return 1;
2928:         if (window.innerWidth <= 900) return 2;
2929:         return 3;
2930:       }
2931: 
2932:       function updateSlider() {
2933:         const visibleCards = getVisibleCards();
2934:         const maxIndex = Math.max(0, cards.length - visibleCards);
2935:         if (currentIndex > maxIndex) currentIndex = maxIndex;
2936: 
2937:         const cardWidth = cards[0].getBoundingClientRect().width;
2938:         const gap = 20;
2939:         const moveAmount = (cardWidth + gap) * currentIndex;
2940:         
2941:         track.style.transform = `translate3d(-${moveAmount}px, 0, 0)`;
2942: 
2943:         dotsContainer.innerHTML = '';
2944:         const totalDots = maxIndex + 1;
2945:         for (let i = 0; i < totalDots; i++) {
2946:           const dot = document.createElement('button');
2947:           dot.className = `tst-dot ${i === currentIndex ? 'active' : ''}`;
2948:           dot.setAttribute('aria-label', `Go to slide ${i + 1}`);
2949:           dot.addEventListener('click', () => {
2950:             currentIndex = i;
2951:             updateSlider();
2952:           });
2953:           dotsContainer.appendChild(dot);
2954:         }
2955:       }
2956: 
2957:       prevBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
2958:         if (currentIndex > 0) {
2959:           currentIndex--;
2960:         } else {
2961:           currentIndex = Math.max(0, cards.length - getVisibleCards());
2962:         }
2963:         updateSlider();
2964:       });
2965: 
2966:       nextBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
2967:         const maxIndex = Math.max(0, cards.length - getVisibleCards());
2968:         if (currentIndex < maxIndex) {
2969:           currentIndex++;
2970:         } else {
2971:           currentIndex = 0;
2972:         }
2973:         updateSlider();
2974:       });
2975: 
2976:       window.addEventListener('resize', updateSlider, { passive: true });
2977:       updateSlider();
2978:     }
2979: 
2980:     // Defer slider init until the testimonials section is actually near the viewport,
2981:     // instead of running it eagerly during initial page load (reduces Total Blocking Time).
2982:     document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
2983:       const section = document.getElementById('testimonials-section');
2984:       if (!section) return;
2985: 
2986:       if ('IntersectionObserver' in window) {
2987:         const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries, obs) => {
2988:           entries.forEach(entry => {
2989:             if (entry.isIntersecting) {
2990:               initTestimonialSlider();
2991:               obs.disconnect();
2992:             }
2993:           });
2994:         }, { rootMargin: '300px 0px' });
2995:         observer.observe(section);
2996:       } else {
2997:         initTestimonialSlider();
2998:       }
2999:     });
3000:   </script>
3001: </section>
